searches.reason: Develop architecture-aware probes of whether recent, repeated interests actually influence rankings. Compare intact histories with recent-item removal, older-item removal, and order shuffling; measure score and top-10 changes, then connect failures to sequence representations and training objectives. Treat perturbations as model sensitivity tests, not evidence of causal user preferences.

searches.reason: Translate qualitative feedback into auditable failure types using only public histories, titles, and descriptions: explicit compatibility conflicts, unsupported prerequisites, possible redundancy, and specific versus broad media matches. Seek annotation methods that distinguish supported judgments from unknown intent, validate against human judgments, and avoid treating purchases as proof of ownership or satisfied demand.

searches.reason: Establish whether inexpensive diagnostic signals predict the actual selection objective. Investigate sampled-negative ranking distortions, training-only chronological replay, popularity and history-length slices, and paired uncertainty estimates across four datasets. Calibrate proposed probes against macro validation HR@10 and the twenty users' full-catalog recommendations while keeping validation and qualitative samples explicitly distinct.
